newsitem.title: POLAND: Michael Jackson said to eye theme park in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Michael Jackson said to eye theme park in Poland.

text.p: American pop star Michael Jackson, due in Poland on Tuesday for a two-day visit, wants to build a Disneyland-style theme park in Warsaw, Polish state television said on Monday.

Jackson is hunting for a site bigger than the Warsaw Zoo for a project worth more than $100 million, the Polish news agency PAP quoted the head of the state Foreign Investment Agency, Waldemar Dabrowski, as saying.
He declined to elaborate, saying it was too early to speak of details, but the television quoted unofficial sources as saying the entertainer hoped to create a theme park.
"(Jackson) is interested in major investments in Warsaw. This will be something magnificent, a big project which may become a great European attraction," Warsaw Mayor Marcin Swiecicki told PAP.
"Jackson's two-day visit will be economic in character, and the signing of concrete contracts is planned."

Jackson was said to be impressed by Poland's growing market of 40 million people and the reception given him on his first visit in September 1996 when 100,000 fans attended his concert at a Warsaw airport.
Spokesmen for Jackson in California were not immediately available for comment on Monday, a holiday in the United States.
Local media said Jackson would fly by helicopter over the capital to view suitable sites. He was also due to tour a historic Warsaw landmarks and visit a children's hospital and a secondary school.
